q: 1. Velocity of flow through porous medium is directly proportional to hydraulic gradient is ...........
explain: Darcy’s Law (v = ki) states that the discharge velocity is proportional to the hydraulic gradient in laminar flow.

q: 2. Coefficient of percolation and coefficient of permeability are related by ...........
explain: Since seepage velocity (vs) = v / n, the coefficient of percolation (Kp) = k / n, where n is porosity.

q: 3. Constant of proportionality between seepage velocity and hydraulic gradient is ...........
explain: The coefficient of percolation (Kp) is specifically associated with the actual seepage velocity through the pores, not the superficial discharge velocity.

q: 4. Capillary water is held in the interstices of soil due to capillarity forces. The capillary forces depends upon ............
explain: Capillary rise is governed by the formula $h = 4\sigma\cos	heta / (\gamma_w d)$. Thus, it depends on surface tension ($\sigma$), pore size (diameter $d$), and the resulting pressure differences.

q: 5. Out of the following, which will have the maximum value of surface tension forces ............
explain: Mercury has a significantly higher surface tension (approximately 480 mN/m) compared to water (72 mN/m) and other common liquids due to strong metallic bonding.

q: 6. The permeability is ............
options: Directly proportional to unit weight, inversely proportional to viscosity
Directly proportional to viscosity, inversely proportional to unit weight
Directly proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
Inversely proportional to both unit weight and viscosity
explain: As per the fundamental permeability equation, higher unit weight increases flow due to gravity, while higher viscosity resists flow, creating an inverse relationship with viscosity.

q: 7. Due to rise in temperature, the unit weight and viscosity of the permeant fluid are reduced to 90% and 60% respectively. If other things remain constant, the coefficient of permeability ............
explain: Since $k \propto \gamma / \mu$, the new permeability $k' = k \cdot (0.9 / 0.6) = 1.5k$. This represents a 50% increase.

q: 8. Units of co-efficient of permeability ............
explain: Coefficient of permeability has the dimensions of velocity ($L/T$), commonly expressed in cm/sec or m/day.

q: 9. In the case of stratified soils, the permeability's Kx and Kz along and across stratification are related as ............
options: no relation between Kx and Kz
explain: In stratified deposits, the equivalent permeability parallel to the layers ($K_x$) is always greater than the equivalent permeability perpendicular to the layers ($K_z$).

q: 10. The range of coefficient of permeability of clay is about ............
explain: Clay is considered practically impervious, with a coefficient of permeability typically less than $10^{-6}$ cm/sec (often reaching $10^{-9}$ cm/sec).

q: 11. The value of coefficient of permeability of sand is ............
explain: Clean sand generally falls within the permeability range of $1$ to $10^{-2}$ cm/sec.

q: 12. Soils with a value for coefficient of permeability ranging between 10⁻⁴ to 10⁻⁶ are classified as ............
explain: Soils with $k$ values between $10^{-4}$ and $10^{-6}$ cm/sec are termed semi-pervious (typical for silts and silty sands).

q: 13. Electrical analogy method is used to ............
options: find the depth to water table
find the water content in a soil
explain: Electrical analogy uses the similarity between Darcy's law and Ohm's law to model seepage and construct flow nets for complex boundary conditions.

q: 14. The shape factor of a flownet is defined as ............
explain: Shape factor ($N_f / N_d$) is the ratio of the number of flow channels to the number of equipotential drops, which is a constant for a given boundary geometry.

q: 15. The u/s face of an earth dam is ............
explain: The upstream face of a dam is submerged and in contact with water of the same potential, making it the first equipotential line ($100\%$ head).

q: 16. Flow through an earth dam is a case of ............
explain: It is unconfined flow because the top boundary of the flow (the phreatic line) is at atmospheric pressure and is not fixed by an impermeable boundary.

q: 17. The phreatic line is ............
options: the u/s face of the earth dam
d/s face of the earth dam
explain: The phreatic line is the seepage line that marks the upper boundary of the saturated zone; it is the top flow line where pressure is atmospheric.

q: 18. The hydrostatic pressure on the phreatic line with in a dam section is ............
explain: By definition, the phreatic line is the locus of points where the pore water pressure is zero (equal to atmospheric pressure).

q: 19. If h is the head of water stored, Nf is the number of flow lines and Nd is the number of equipotential drops in a flow net, then the seepage flow rate is given by ............
explain: The standard discharge formula from a flow net is $q = k \cdot H \cdot (N_f / N_d)$, where $H$ is the total head causing flow.

q: 20. A flow net may be used for the determination of ............
explain: Flow nets are a graphical representation used to calculate all hydraulic parameters including discharge ($q$), uplift pressure at any point, and the gradient at the exit.

q: 21. The seepage velocity vs and the Darcy's velocity v are related as ............
explain: Since water only flows through the voids, the actual velocity ($v_s$) is higher than the discharge velocity ($v$). It is related by porosity ($n$) as $v_s = v/n$.

q: 22. An isobar is ............
options: a curve connecting points of equal vertical pressure
a point at which the net pressure is zero
a curve connecting points of equal horizontal pressure
a curve connecting points of equal pore water pressure
explain: An isobar (or 'pressure bulb') is a contour line that joins points of equal vertical stress increment in the soil mass below a loaded area.

q: 23. Consolidation theory was enunciated by ............
explain: Karl Terzaghi, the father of soil mechanics, developed the one-dimensional consolidation theory in 1923 to explain how saturated clays settle over time.

q: 24. The unit of the coefficient of consolidation is ............
explain: The coefficient of consolidation ($C_v$) is defined by the units of Area/Time ($L^2/T$), typically $cm^2/sec$ or $m^2/year$.

q: 25. Direct measurement of permeability of the soil specimen can be made at any stage of loading in ............
explain: In a floating ring consolidometer, the ring is free to move, reducing friction and allowing for better drainage setups that facilitate direct permeability measurements during the test.

q: 26. The expression for vertical stress at a point below the corner of a rectangular loaded area was derived by ............
explain: Newmark derived the integration of Boussinesq's equation specifically for a point under the corner of a rectangular area, leading to the use of 'Influence Charts'.

q: 27. Newmark's chart is based on the concept of vertical stress under ............
explain: Newmark’s Influence Chart is constructed using the equation for vertical stress at the center of a uniformly loaded circular area.

q: 28. Effective stress is ...............
options: the stress at the particles contact
governing factor for the engineering properties of the soil
explain: Effective stress represents the actual pressure transmitted through soil grain contacts. It is a fundamental physical parameter that controls soil strength and deformation.
